_説明: Explanations shown when you click a word in the code (English). tools/make_glossaries.py makes this file from the dictionaries in tools/glossary/en/ (fix the dictionaries, not this file).
$ ping: Checks whether the other side can be reached and how many ms a round trip takes (ICMP)
$ ping -c: Number of times to send (otherwise it runs until you press Ctrl+C)
$ dig +trace: Shows the lookup step by step from the root servers
$ dig AAAA: Looks up the IPv6 address (AAAA record)
$ dig MX: Looks up the servers that receive email (MX records)
$ dig @8.8.8.8: Chooses which DNS server to ask (here Google's 8.8.8.8)
$ dig @1.1.1.1: Chooses which DNS server to ask (here Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1)
$ tracepath: Finds the routers on the way to the other side, one by one
$ tracepath -n: Prints IP addresses without turning them into names
$ mtr: Keeps measuring delay and lost packets at each router on the way
$ mtr -n: Prints IP addresses without turning them into names
$ mtr -r: Stops after a set number of rounds and prints a report
$ ip: Shows and changes network settings (addresses, routes, neighbors)
$ ip addr: Shows IP addresses (same as ip a)
$ ip a: Shows IP addresses (same as ip addr)
$ ip neigh: Shows the neighbors' MAC addresses learned through ARP
$ ip link: Shows whether LAN ports and Wi-Fi are connected
$ ip -br: Brief output: one line per interface
$ ss: Shows current connections and ports being listened on
$ ss -tn: Shows TCP connections as numbers rather than names
$ ss -tlnp: Shows listening (l) TCP ports with process names (p)
$ nc: Connects over TCP or UDP to send and receive text (netcat)
$ nc -N: Close the connection once sending is done
$ nc -zv: Send no data; just check whether the port is open and report
$ curl -v: Shows in detail what was sent and received (headers, the encryption greeting)
$ curl -w: What to print when finished (%{http_code} prints the status code)
$ resolvectl: Shows and controls DNS on Ubuntu (systemd-resolved)
$ resolvectl status: Shows the DNS servers in use now
$ nmcli: Controls NetworkManager (Wi-Fi lists, signal strength and more)
$ ufw: Sets up the firewall on Ubuntu
$ ufw default: Decide what to do with traffic no rule matches
$ tcpdump: Prints the packets flowing past, one by one
$ tcpdump -n: Prints IP addresses and port numbers without turning them into names
$ tcpdump -i: Which interface to watch (any means all)
$ iperf3: Measures how fast data can be sent between two machines
$ iperf3 -s: Wait as the side being measured (server)
$ iperf3 -c: The measuring side (client). Write the other machine's IP address after it
$ ssh -L: Makes a tunnel from a local port to a port on the remote side
$ ssh -i: Which private key file to use
$ mosquitto_sub: Subscribes to MQTT topics and prints the messages that arrive
$ mosquitto_pub: Publishes a message to an MQTT topic
$ mosquitto_sub -t: The topic (+ and # can be used)
mqtt: paho-mqtt's MQTT client module (import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt)
paho: An MQTT client library (pip install paho-mqtt)
mqtt.Client: Creates an MQTT client (the thing that connects to the broker)
CallbackAPIVersion: Which argument style the callback functions (on_connect etc.) use. VERSION2 is the new style
VERSION2: Call back with the new argument style from paho-mqtt 2
on_connect: A function called when connected to the broker
on_message: A function called when a message arrives on a subscribed topic
connect: Connects to the broker (host name and port number)
subscribe: Asks the broker to send you a topic's messages
publish: Sends a message to a topic
qos: The delivery promise: 0 send and forget, 1 at least once, 2 exactly once
loop_forever: Keeps handling communication forever (does not return until stopped)
loop_start: Starts handling communication in a background thread
wait_for_publish: Waits until the message has been sent to the broker
payload: The message contents (bytes; decode() turns them into text)
reason_code: The result of connecting (Success means it worked)
userdata: A value you can choose to pass along (None if unused)
dumps: Turns a Python value into JSON text
import: Loads a module (another file or library). You can give it a short name with as, as in import numpy as np
from: Loads only part of a module. from datetime import date
as: Gives another name to something imported, or something opened with with
def: Makes a function. After def name(arguments):, write the body indented
for: Takes the contents of a container one at a time and repeats
in: In for, "one at a time from..."; in a condition, "whether it is in..."
or: True when at least one is true
range: Makes a run of integers. range(5) is 0–4, range(1, 6) is 1–5
list: Makes a list (an ordered, changeable container)
set: Makes a set (a container with no duplicates)
round: Rounds (to the nearest even number at .5). round(x, 1) gives 1 decimal place
pi: π, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter
sleep: Waits for the given number of seconds
json: A module for reading and writing JSON files
pip: The tool for installing Python libraries
$ sudo:
Origin: short for superuser do (run as the administrator).
Runs the following command with administrator rights. Needed to change system settings or install software.
It asks for your password the first time (nothing appears on screen as you type).
$ apt:
Origin: short for Advanced Package Tool.
The command that manages software on Ubuntu. It installs and removes software.
$ apt install:
Installs software from the internet.
Example: sudo apt install pipx installs pipx.
$ ssh:
Origin: short for Secure Shell.
Logs in to a computer across the network. git also uses it to talk to GitHub.
$ ssh-keygen:
Origin: short for key generator.
Makes an SSH key (a pair of a private key and a public key). It can also delete the stored key of a host you connected to (-R), among other things.
$ ssh-keygen -t:
Origin: -t is short for type.
Chooses the type of key. ed25519 is recommended today.
$ ssh-keygen -N:
Origin: -N stands for new passphrase.
Sets the passphrase. -N "" makes it empty (you are not asked).
$ pi@raspberrypi.local:
The form "username@computer-name". Connects to raspberrypi.local as the user pi.
With scp, write the destination path after the : that follows.
$ &&:
If the previous command succeeded, runs the next one.
git add . && git commit -m "…" is the same as typing the two in order.
$ apt update: Refreshes the list of software (which versions are available). Do it before apt install
Loads a settings file into the current terminal (the same as source)
$ |:
Origin: a pipe, like data flowing through a pipe.
Passes the result of the command on the left to the command on the right.
$ python3:
Origin: version 3 of Python.
Runs a Python program on the PC.
$ echo:
Origin: an echo.
Outputs the text you write as it is.
$ pip:
Origin: said to be short for pip installs packages.
Installs Python libraries. It cannot be used on the Pico.
$ apt upgrade: Updates the installed software to newer versions.
$ python3 -m: Runs a Python module as a command. python3 -m serial.tools.miniterm runs pyserial's serial monitor.
$ python3 -c: Runs the following string as Python code
$ apt -y: Answers "yes" automatically (does not ask for confirmation)
$ apt install -y: Answers "yes" automatically (does not ask for confirmation)
$ curl: Downloads data from a URL (also used to call web APIs)
$ curl -o: Sets the file name to save to
